title: IPFS MCP A2UI catalog
description: IPFS components for an agent that operates the person's own Kubo node. Generated from mcp/ui; do not edit. Regenerate with `pnpm gen:catalog`.
instructions: IPFS components for an agent that operates the person's own Kubo node. Each view component draws the structured output of one MCP tool: set `tool` to the tool name and bind `output` to the data model path that holds the tool's structuredContent. Output that does not match the tool's schema is not drawn. Write and destructive tools always pass a confirmation first: use ApprovalCard or ConfirmationDialog to show it, and wire approveAction only when this surface can really approve. Never imply an action ran before it did.

label.description: A short string, typically 1 to 3 words, used by assistive technologies to convey the purpose or intent of an element. For example, an input field might have an accessible label of 'User ID' or a button might be labeled 'Submit'.

description.description: Additional information provided by assistive technologies about an element such as instructions, format requirements, or result of an action. For example, a mute button might have a label of 'Mute' and a description of 'Silences notifications about this conversation'.

Action.description: Defines an interaction handler that can either trigger a server-side event or execute a local client-side function.

event.description: The event to dispatch to the server.

name.description: The name of the action to be dispatched to the server.

context.description: A JSON object containing the key-value pairs for the action context. Values can be literals or paths. Use literal values unless the value must be dynamically bound to the data model. Do NOT use paths for static IDs.

ComponentId.description: The unique identifier for a component, used for both definitions and references within the same surface.

path.description: A JSON Pointer path to a value in the data model.

DynamicBoolean.description: A boolean value that can be a literal, a path, or a function call returning a boolean.

DynamicStringList.description: Represents a value that can be either a literal array of strings, a path to a string array in the data model, or a function call returning a string array.

DynamicValue.description: A value that can be a literal, a path, or a function call returning any type.

FunctionCall.description: Invokes a named function on the client.

call.description: The name of the function to call.

returnType.description: The expected return type of the function call.

ipfs_Cid.description: A CID in any multibase Kubo accepts (CIDv0 base58btc or CIDv1, for example bafy...).

ipfs_ContentPath.description: A bare CID, a CID with a sub-path, or an /ipfs/, /ipns/ or /ipld/ content path. No segment may be . or .., so path cleaning cannot change the namespace or the root a caller checked (R13 security L2).

ipfs_Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned as next_cursor by a previous call. Clients must not parse it.

ipfs_Encoding.description: How content bytes are carried in a JSON string.

ipfs_IpnsName.description: An IPNS name (libp2p-key CID or DNSLink domain), with or without the /ipns/ prefix. The name may not start with a dot, and no sub-path segment may be . or .. (R13 security L2).

ipfs_KeyName.description: The local name of a keystore key, for example self.

ipfs_MfsCopySource.description: An MfsPath, or an /ipfs/<cid>[/path] content path. /ipns/ and /ipld/ sources are rejected, and no segment may be . or .. (R13 security L2).

ipfs_MfsPath.description: An absolute path in the node's Mutable File System (MFS). Paths under /ipfs/, /ipns/ and /ipld/ are rejected: the daemon would resolve them as content paths, letting a closed-world MFS tool read from the network. Copy content into MFS with mfs_cp, whose source is an MfsCopySource. A segment equal to . or .. is rejected, and so is an empty first segment (//): path cleaning would otherwise turn /a/../ipns/x or //ipfs/x into a content path (R13 security L2). Bare /ipfs, /ipns and /ipld name ordinary MFS entries.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor to fetch the next page. Present only when has_more is true.

ipfs_PageInfo.description: Cursor pagination metadata for list tools.

ipfs_PeerId.description: A libp2p peer ID (base58btc or CIDv1 libp2p-key).

uri.description: An ipfs:// or ipns:// resource URI readable with resources/read.

mime_type.description: Detected or declared media type, when known.

ipfs_ResourceRef.description: A resource the client reads separately instead of receiving it inline (sent as an MCP resource_link content block as well).

ipfs_Warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings about work that follows the tool's own effect, which has already succeeded: for example index entries kept because the pin check or the vector store failed. Absent when there is nothing to report. The tool's result is unchanged by them.

ipfs_confirmation_ConfirmationRequired.description: Carried in ToolError.error.confirmation. code confirmation_required: a new pending confirmation was created; code confirmation_pending: a token or retry arrived while it is still pending. Repeating the call never approves it; only a resolver in resolvers does.

state.description: Approved confirmations never appear here: an approved call runs.

resolvers.description: Human-presence resolvers that may approve this confirmation, in order of preference. Never contains token.

confirm_token.description: Binding handle for sessions of kind human-mcp that cannot elicit: after a resolver approves, repeat the same call with this token to run it exactly once. Rejected (confirmation_pending, confirmation_declined or confirmation_expired) unless the confirmation is approved. Never present for principals of kind a2a or uar.

requires_native_prompt.description: Same meaning as PendingConfirmation.requires_native_prompt: true for destructive calls from the ui and a2a principals (ADR-0003 Round 7 amendment). Only a presence resolver (macos-localauth or linux-polkit) decides; desktop does not count until a Desktop confirmation window consumes the pairing key (it still resolves write-class confirmations), and cli and agui-interrupt never do, and with no presence resolver available the call is refused with confirmation_unavailable. An in-chat surface must not offer an approve control and may only offer deny. Absent means false.

ipfs_confirmation_Resolver.description: Human-presence mechanisms. The confirm token is deliberately not a resolver.

ipfs_confirmation_Summary.description: What the user is asked to approve. text is rendered from the catalog confirmationSummary template and names the CID, path or name affected.

mode.description: dark (default), light, or follow the system setting.
